hero.title: Engineering physical systems from the package outward.
hero.description: Mechanical engineering student with hands-on experience in vehicle low-voltage systems, industrial panel assembly, manufacturing quality, asset integrity, and engineering automation. I work across the details that make a design buildable, testable, serviceable, and documented.

image.alt: Ashwin Conrad holding a Formula EV low-voltage electrical enclosure during competition preparation

facts: Low Voltage Electronics Lead · Formula EV Racing

profile.heading: Mechanical engineering first. Systems thinking in practice.
profile.lead: My work starts with the physical system: how it fits, how it is built, how it is accessed, how it behaves in use, and how the people around it can diagnose and improve it.
profile.body: Electrical integration, data tooling, and technical documentation extend that mechanical foundation. Across Formula EV, industrial controls, and asset-integrity work, I have worked where packaging, hardware, manufacturing, testing, data, and communication meet.

signals.label: DESIGN WITH THE BUILD IN MIND
signals.text: Vehicle packaging, panel drawings, physical assembly, and fabrication projects keep the practical constraints visible early.

signals.label: CLOSE THE LOOP WITH TESTING
signals.text: QA checks, troubleshooting, inspection planning, and operating-data analysis turn observations into engineering decisions.

signals.label: MAKE THE WORK TRANSFERABLE
signals.text: Diagrams, scope packages, dashboards, and repeatable tools help technicians, operations teams, and other engineers use the result.

case_studies.title: Formula UA27 low-voltage systems
case_studies.subtitle: Vehicle electrical integration shaped by packaging, safety interfaces, accessibility, and team coordination.

image.alt: Formula UA27 at its unveiling, showing the full vehicle context for low-voltage electrical integration

case_studies.objective: Plan and integrate the low-voltage system for Formula UA27 around the vehicle package, including power distribution, control hardware, sensors, and safety interfaces.
case_studies.context: Formula EV work requires electrical decisions to coexist with the chassis, vehicle packaging, team schedule, and the practical need to inspect and service the car.
case_studies.contribution: Lead low-voltage electrical system planning and integration; coordinate board-level hardware, safety interfaces, sensor integration, and power-distribution work with mechanical and software teammates.

decision.label: ENGINEERING FOCUS
decision.title: Treat the electrical system as part of the vehicle package.
decision.text: Low-voltage work is not isolated from the mechanical system. Component placement, access, and integration are considered alongside the electrical function so the team can build, inspect, and troubleshoot the vehicle as a complete system.

results: Current subsystem leadership role for Formula UA27.
Coordinates low-voltage planning across board-level hardware, sensors, safety interfaces, and vehicle packaging.

case_studies.title: Brazed aluminum heat-exchanger lifecycle analysis
case_studies.subtitle: Operating data, OEM limits, and field context combined to support risk-based decisions on aging process equipment.

image.alt: AltaGas field inspection team examining facility equipment

case_studies.objective: Assess fatigue risk and monitoring gaps for brazed aluminum heat exchangers using historical operating data and OEM-prescribed operating limits.
case_studies.context: The equipment supports facility operations, so the analysis had to connect historical process behaviour with inspection planning and practical operational awareness.
case_studies.contribution: Extracted process data with the PI Historian Excel add-in and developed Python screening tools for thermal ramp rates, cyclic operation limits, and parting-sheet temperature distributions.

decision.label: ENGINEERING DECISION
decision.title: Use measured operating behaviour to focus the next action.
decision.text: The work connected process data with failure mechanisms and monitoring coverage. Recommendations included additional instrumentation where coverage was insufficient and reduced actuated-valve opening rates to limit turbulent flow and erosion on the inner pipe face.

results: Analyzed 2+ years of data across 12+ brazed aluminum heat exchangers.
Compiled lifecycle findings for leadership to support risk-based decision-making and inspection planning.

figures.alt: Field inspection activity around AltaGas equipment
figures.caption: Figure 03 — Field context for the asset data. Engineering analysis is stronger when it remains connected to the equipment, inspection work, and operating decisions it supports.

case_studies.title: Control panel builds and pre-delivery quality
case_studies.subtitle: Drawing interpretation, panel assembly, wiring, software loading, and quality checks in an industrial manufacturing environment.

image.alt: Open electrical control panel with internal wiring and industrial hardware

case_studies.objective: Build, wire, load, and check industrial control panels from engineering drawings through pre-delivery quality assurance.
case_studies.context: The work required precision at the component level while maintaining the broader delivery context: documented designs, repeatable build processes, quality expectations, and technician teamwork.
case_studies.contribution: Interpreted panel designs and electrical schematics; assembled and wired control panels; loaded control-module software; completed pre-delivery QA; and resolved quality-control deficiencies before customer delivery.

decision.label: MANUFACTURING LESSON
decision.title: A panel is not complete when the last conductor is landed.
decision.text: The build also has to be checked against the documentation and prepared for the next person who will inspect, ship, install, or diagnose it. This perspective translates directly to serviceable product development.

results: Built, wired, loaded, and checked a sample of 30+ control panels across individual and team builds.
Processed 250+ PLC software updates in under half the allocated time while supporting panel production and QA.
